newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SOUTH AUSTRALIA TO REFUND LIQUOR FEES.
newsitem.headline: SOUTH AUSTRALIA TO REFUND LIQUOR FEES.

text.p: The South Australian government said on Tuesday it would refund certain liquor licence fees in the wake of the High Court's decision on state levies.

Premier John Olsen said in a statement the government would reimburse licensees the equivalent of 60.87 percent of the liquor licence fee paid for the September quarter 1997, with an estimated A$7 million impact on the state budget over two years.

The federal government has agreed to levy around A$5 billion of alcohol, tobacco and petrol taxes on behalf of the six states and two territories and return the money to them following last week's High Court decision which effectively outlawed them.
The states became embroiled in a row with industry over whether some of the outlawed taxes were paid in advance and how to ensure prices remained steady.

Olsen said South Australian maintained the liquor franchise fees which had been paid had been calculated on past sales and not prepaid on future sales, but had reached agreement with the industry after a call by Treasurer Peter Costello for the refunds.
